intro.title: Customer Relationship Management
paragraphs: Your dream is to become a successful entrepreneur and create a business that brings people together.
You have just been hired by a large multinational company where people from different cultures, backgrounds, and professions work together.

Today you enter the Customer Service Department, where things are a bit chaotic. A colleague is struggling with an angry customer, the filing cabinet has exploded, and a feedback survey needs finishing. Time to put your Customer Relationship Management skills to work!

dialogues.intro1: I tried helping this customer… But he started screaming at me. He keeps saying I'm bad at my job…
dialogues.intro2: No matter what I say, he won't calm down. I'm just making it worse.
dialogues.intro3: Can you please take over the call?
dialogues.default: Thanks for helping with that call…

dialogues.intro1: Oh, there you are! I'm making feedback survey for our customers, but I need some help...
dialogues.intro2: I've drafted a bunch of questions. I think some are good… but some are, well… terrible.
dialogues.intro3: Can you help me choose which questions to use in the survey? I'll show you two at a time.
dialogues.default: Let me know if you need anything else!

complaintCall.title: The Customer Complaint Call
complaintCall.instructions: Navigate the phone call with a frustrated customer. Choose your responses wisely — the customer's mood depends on it.
complaintCall.holdWarning: Warning: Putting the customer on hold will lower their mood significantly!
complaintCall.holdResponse: I can't believe they put me on hold! Hello? Helloooo?
complaintCall.holdReturn: Thanks for waiting. Let's continue. Where were we?
complaintCall.holdFailure: You know what? Forget it. I'm done.

stages.customerStatement: Hi. Your colleague said you could help me. I've been trying to get in contact for days!

options.good: I'm really sorry it's been so hard to reach us. I understand how frustrating that must be. I'm here to help you now.
options.neutral: I see. I can help you now.
options.bad: Well, we've been very busy lately. That's probably why you haven't gotten through.

customerReplies.good: Thank you. I've been feeling pretty ignored!
customerReplies.neutral: Okay… I just hope someone actually helps me this time.
customerReplies.bad: Ok… But I've been waiting for days…

userFollowUp.good: I understand. Let's go over what's been happening and get things sorted out.
userFollowUp.neutral: Let's go over what's been happening.
userFollowUp.bad: Ok, tell me what the problem is.

stages.customerStatement: My order hasn't been shipped! It was supposed to be a birthday gift, but now it might not arrive in time!

options.good: I understand that this is frustrating. Let's go through it together and see what we can do.
options.bad: You don't need to get worked up!

customerReplies.good: Thank you for actually listening to me.
customerReplies.neutral: Yeah… I guess. I just want to know what's going on.

userFollowUp.good: Of course. Let's take this step by step.

stages.customerStatement: So what actually happened to my order?

options.good: I'll look it up right now. Could you confirm your order number, so I check the right details?
options.neutral: I can check. What's the order number?
options.bad: You'll get it eventually. You just have to be patient.

customerReplies.bad: That's not good enough. I need to know! Please check my order number 38492!

userFollowUp.good: Thank you. I'll check that immediately.
userFollowUp.neutral: Alright, let me pull that up.

options.good: Yes. I see there was a delay from the warehouse. I'll check the shipment update and keep you posted.
options.neutral: Yes. I see that it's delayed. I'll look at the latest update.
options.bad: Yeah, it's delayed. Not my fault.

customerReplies.neutral: Okay. I just want to know what's happening.
customerReplies.bad: You're not taking any responsibility? Great.

userFollowUp.good: I'll make sure you get the latest information.

options.good: I'll keep an eye on the shipment and update you as soon as anything changes.
options.neutral: We just need to wait for the next tracking update.
options.bad: It comes when it comes. You should've ordered earlier if timing was important.

customerReplies.neutral: Okay… I guess there's nothing else to do.
customerReplies.bad: Wow… that's very rude! Your website stated it would arrive within 3 business days!

userFollowUp.good: I'll make sure you stay informed.
userFollowUp.neutral: I'll let you know if I see anything new.
userFollowUp.bad: You have to be patient. There's nothing else we can do.

options.good: Before we end the call, is there anything else you'd like our assistance with today?
options.neutral: Yes, that's all the information I have for now.
options.bad: If that's everything, I'm going to end the call now.

customerReplies.good: No, that's all. Thanks for taking the time to help me!
customerReplies.neutral: Alright… I hope it comes soon. Bye.

userFollowUp.good: I'm happy to help. Thanks for calling and have a great day.

failure.title: Call Ended
failure.message:
Your customer hung up due to poor service.

To give customers a better experience:
• Stay calm and patient
• Listen to the customer and acknowledge their feelings
• Apologize and take ownership of the situation
• Be clear and solution-oriented
• Follow through on promises
• Avoid hold whenever possible

success.title: Well Done!
success.message:
Congratulations, you handled that call well!

You stayed calm and listened actively. You took ownership of the situation by apologizing and offering a concrete solution. This made the customer feel seen and heard, leading to a positive resolution of the situation.

customerRegistry.title: The Chaotic Customer Registry
customerRegistry.instructions: Sort through the customer records. Drag each data entry into the correct column: Keep or Erase.
customerRegistry.thought2: Well… organizing the customer records has been on my to do-list for a while. I better get to it.

privacyGuidelines.title: What counts as personal data?
privacyGuidelines.content:
Any information related to a specific person. Examples:
• Name, address, phone number, email address
• National Identification Number
• Credit card information, payment details
• Internet Protocol (IP) address
• Notes about customers

And many more… If it can identify someone, it is personal data!

privacyGuidelines.title: Special (extra sensitive!) data
privacyGuidelines.content:
Handle with extreme care:
• Race and ethnic origin
• Political, religious and philosophical beliefs
• Trade union membership
• Health and genetics
• Biometrics (like fingerprints or retina scans)
• Sex life and sexual orientation

privacyGuidelines.title: Processing means
privacyGuidelines.content: Anything you do with personal data: collecting, storing, updating, deleting, sharing

privacyGuidelines.title: Survival rules for data processing (GDPR principles)
privacyGuidelines.content:
• Have a proper reason (lawful basis)
• Be fair, not harmful or misleading
• Tell people clearly what you're doing
• Do not reuse data for other purposes
• Keep only what you need
• Keep it accurate and up to date
• Delete it when you're done
• Keep it safe
• Be able to prove you follow these rules

privacyGuidelines.title: Lawful basis – why are we allowed to keep the data?
privacyGuidelines.content:
1. Consent — Customer said "yes" to data processing. Used for: newsletters, loyalty programs, marketing
2. Contract — We need it to fulfil contract obligations. Used for: orders, deliveries, refunds
3. Legal Obligation — The law makes us keep it. Used for: invoices, receipts, accounting records, tax documentations
4. Legitimate Interest — We need it to run the business. Important: it must not be harmful for the customer. Used for: B2B contact details, factual customer service notes

completion.title: Customer Registry Sorted!
completion.message:
Congratulations! You successfully sorted the customer registry.

All the information you kept was covered by a legal basis:
• Contract: information needed to fulfil customer requests, deliver products, resolve complaints, manage warranties, and maintain business agreements.
• Legal obligation: invoices, receipts, and consent records required by law to store
• Legitimate interest: factual and useful information for running a business
• Consent: additional data obtained through clear and written consent

Breaching GDPR and privacy laws could be harmful for the business. Thankfully, you erased all inaccurate, misplaced, subjective, discriminatory, duplicate and irrelevant information.

An up-to-date customer registry helps protect our customer's privacy and build trust. Well done!

feedbackSurvey.title: The Customer Feedback Survey
feedbackSurvey.instructions: Help Simone build a good feedback survey. For each pair, choose the better question to include.

questions.correct: How easy was it to find the information you needed on our website?
questions.wrong: What is your favourite holiday destination?
questions.explanation:
Ask relevant questions.
A question about holiday destinations is irrelevant and will not provide any useful feedback. It can also be confusing and distracting for the respondent.

questions.correct: How satisfied were you with the product you purchased?
questions.wrong: How satisfied were you with the fantastic product you purchased?
questions.explanation:
Ask neutral questions.
Calling the product "fantastic" makes the question leading. This can influence the customer's response.

questions.correct: How satisfied were you with our customer support services?
questions.wrong: If you had contacted our customer support team, and they had been extremely responsive to your requests, would you recommend our business to your friends and family?
questions.explanation:
Ask about actual experiences.
In general, hypothetical questions will provide feedback that is uncertain and difficult to act upon.

questions.correct: How would you rate your overall experience today?
questions.wrong: Considering the interplay between our website, chat, phone and email support services… how would you evaluate our performance?
questions.explanation:
Ask clear and straightforward questions.
Long and complex questions can overwhelm the respondent.

Use rating scales to get more detailed data.
Experiences and opinions will often be on spectrum of positive and negative. Yes/no questions can oversimplify and hide nuances.

questions.correct: How did you first hear about us? Search Engines / Social Media / Referral / Customer Review site / Internet Ad / Newspaper Ad / Other
questions.wrong: How did you first hear about us? Search Engines / Social Media
questions.explanation:
Include all relevant answering options. Include "other" or "I don't know" options.
Otherwise, respondents can be forced to select an inaccurate option, skip the question or abandon the survey.

questions.correct: How satisfied were you with the product you purchased?
questions.wrong: How satisfied were you with the product and the customer service?
questions.explanation:
Focus at one topic per question.
Asking about two different things in the same question can lead to inaccurate and unclear feedback.

questions.correct: What could we improve about our delivery services?
questions.wrong: Do you like our brand colours?
questions.explanation:
Keep the goal of the survey in mind (customer experiences).
Ask questions that will provide concrete feedback on the matter at hand.

questions.correct: How easy was the checkout process?
questions.wrong: Why were you so confused during checkout?
questions.explanation:
Use respectful language.
Avoid accusatory questions that can make respondents feel uncomfortable.

feedbackSurvey.allCorrectMessage: Perfect! All your survey questions are well-crafted.
feedbackSurvey.someWrongMessage: Some questions could be improved. Click on the red questions for explanations.

rubberDuck.title: Rubber Duck
rubberDuck.text: Are you stuck? Explaining the problem out loud might help you solve it. The duck is here to listen!

notebook.title: Notebook
notebook.text:
A notebook to keep track on customers? It can be a good start when you run a small business.

Writing down important information makes it easier to follow up on promises and complaints, remember preferences and offer more personalized experiences.

You can move on to spreadsheets or a digital Customer Relationship Management (CRM) system when you feel more comfortable.
